subject: Recovery window, liability and routing policy for multi-region DR
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finlogix.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@finlogix.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify recovery windows + routing expectations for EU/US coverage

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance and the routing options looked promising. Before we move to signature we need to validate a couple of items from our risk and platform teams so Legal can complete redlines:

1) Recovery time objective / recovery point objective: our requirement is RTO <= 3 hours and RPO <= 15 minutes for cross-region failover (US <-> EU). Is Redwood able to commit to that in the SLA (or accept a carveout with explicit mitigation steps)?

2) Routing & activation: we need an explicit description of who initiates failover (Redwood automated detection vs customer-requested manual switchover), detection windows you rely on, and whether DNS or anycast routing is used for cross-region traffic.

3) Latency during normal ops vs during failover: our SREs expect p95 serving latency <= 200ms within-region; during failover we accept higher latency but need a cap (we currently propose p95 <= 1s for the first 2 hours post-failover).

4) Liability & SLA credits for cross-region events: FinLogix is sensitive to broad blackouts that impact downstream SLAs. We need the failure credits calculation to be explicit for failover events (including any warm-standby activation windows).

I've attached our requirement matrix (FinLogix_RTO_RPO_requirements_v2.pdf) and the draft SLA redlines. Can you confirm your position on the RTO/RPO, routing responsibility, and propose language we can push to Legal?

Also if you have an operational diagram showing warm vs cold standby and how traffic is shifted, please attach.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are targeting procurement sign-off by 05/20.

Best,
Samir
Director of Platform Reliability
FinLogix

Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify recovery windows + routing expectations for EU/US coverage

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: we can meet the operational objectives you outlined with a small set of contract clarifications and an agreed-on operational runbook. Details below and attached: SLA-draft-redlines.docx and a failover diagram (redwood-failover-diagram.png).

RTO/RPO
- Proposed contract language: Redwood commits to an operational RTO of <= 2 hours for warm-standby cross-region failover when warm capacity is configured and continuously synced. Where customers opt for cold-standby (lower-cost reserved capacity), RTO is 6 hours.
- RPO: when prefix/KV cache syncing is enabled, RPO <= 15 minutes. If a customer disables cross-region KV replication for cost reasons, RPO will be listed as best-effort and not guaranteed.

Routing and activation
- Detection: automated health checks + circuit-breaker logic detect region-level degradation. Detection window is typically 3–10 minutes depending on the failure mode; the runbook uses a 10-minute detection/verification window before automated canary failover.
- Failover initiation options: customer-configurable. We support (a) automatic failover with automated canary traffic, (b) manual failover initiated by customer via Console API, and (c) a hybrid canary-then-cutover mode.
- Network routing: primary mechanism is anycast edge with region-aware routing. For explicit cutover we provide a signed DNS toggle and an API to update routing policy; we’ll document DNS TTL recommendations (60s) in the runbook.

Normal vs failover latency
- Baseline: p95 <= 200ms within-region under agreed capacity profile.
- Failover: objective is p95 <= 1s for the first 2 hours post-activation when warm-standby is used; beyond that the SLA reverts to per-region availability for the active region.

Liability & credits
- For cross-region failover events that meet the SLA definitions (unplanned region outage and failed automated recovery within RTO), Redwood proposes the same credit formula used for region availability (monthly uptime percentage) with an addendum that caps cumulative credits related to a single cross-region incident at 3x monthly recurring charges for the affected services.

Operational prerequisites
- Warm-standby requires cross-region KV replication, reserved capacity for standby nodes, and an agreed data retention/replication policy.
- We will provide runbook pages, playbook triggers and a pre-approved rollback strategy assigned to both parties.

Next steps
- I attached a marked-up SLA draft (SLA-draft-redlines.docx) with the RTO/RPO language and a failover diagram. Monica, can your team confirm the deployment and billing delta for enabling warm-standby for FinLogix?
- Kimberly, legal: please review the proposed cap on credits and the opt-in terms for warm vs cold standby.

If that aligns with FinLogix’s needs we can produce a final redline for Legal and a Service Activation checklist to sign off the operational prerequisites.

— Vivek
VP, Customer & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

[attachments: SLA-draft-redlines.docx, redwood-failover-diagram.png]

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: FinLogix RTO/RPO proposal — legal & infra confirmation needed

Kimberly / Aditya — looping you in on the FinLogix thread. Highlights: they asked for RTO <= 3h and RPO <= 15m. I proposed: RTO 2h for warm-standby, 6h for cold-standby; RPO 15m with KV-sync enabled. Also proposed credit cap = 3x MRC for a single incident.

Please confirm:
- Legal: is the credit cap language acceptable or do we need to propose a dollar cap with carveouts for catastrophic events? Also confirm that the "detection window" language (10-minute verification prior to automated canary) is defensible.
- Infra: can we guarantee the 3–10 minute detection window and the 2-hour warm-standby activation for FinLogix traffic profile? If we need a narrower capacity presumption (e.g., minimum reserved qps or token throughput) call it out so we can add it to the activation checklist.

We expect Procurement target 05/20, and we need these confirmations to finalize the SLA redline.

Thanks,
Vivek

[internal only — no attachments]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finlogix.com>

Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify recovery windows + routing expectations for EU/US coverage

Vivek — thanks for the quick and detailed response. The proposed RTO/RPO pair for warm-standby (2h / 15m) is acceptable to our SREs provided we have:

- A signed Service Activation checklist that enumerates the required capacity and KV replication configuration (we need the checklist before live traffic).
- Explicit DNS TTL recommendations and a rollback trigger documented.
- A concrete example in the runbook showing a simulated failover sequence and associated timelines (detection, canary, full cutover).

Regarding credits: Finance prefers a dollar cap in addition to the 3x MRC cap — can you propose a plug number? For example, FinLogix would accept a $250k per-incident cap tied to services covered under the agreement. If you can't accept a dollar cap, we need clearer language around catastrophic events and force majeure carveouts.

Please send the Service Activation checklist and updated SLA redline (we reviewed SLA-draft-redlines.docx and left a couple of inline comments). If you can get us a final redline and activation checklist by EOD Friday 05/15, we will route to Procurement and Legal for signature.

Appreciate it.
Samir
